title: Coupling and Cohesion
body:
The most load-bearing pair of ideas in the course. Every other quality argument reduces to
one of these two.

- **Coupling** is dependence *between* modules. **Low is good.**
- **Cohesion** is how single-purpose a module is *inside*. **High is good.**

They pull in the same direction. A module that does one thing needs less from its neighbours,
so raising cohesion usually lowers coupling by itself. The failure mode is the same in both
directions: a change in one place forces changes in several others, which is exactly what
makes the [[SDLC]] maintenance phase expensive.

## Why it is the whole game

Software does not get hard because any one function is hard. It gets hard because everything
touches everything else, so nobody can predict what a change will break. Coupling is the name
for that. Both design paradigms exist to control it: the [[Structured Approach]] by
decomposing into functions, the [[Object Oriented Approach]] by decomposing into objects that
hide their data. [[Encapsulation]], [[Interface]] versus [[Implementation]],
[[Polymorphism]], and [[Abstraction]] are all mechanisms for the same goal.

## Coupling, worst to best

| Kind | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Content** | one module reaches into another's internals directly |
| **Common** | several modules share global data ([[global variable]] is the classic) |
| **Control** | one module passes a flag telling another *how* to behave |
| **Stamp** | a whole record is passed when only one field is used |
| **Data** | only the parameters actually needed are passed |

Data coupling is the target. The test that catches most of it: can you understand this module
without opening the other one?

## Cohesion, worst to best

| Kind | What holds the module together |
|---|---|
| **Coincidental** | nothing (`utils.java`) |
| **Logical** | same category of thing, selected by a flag |
| **Temporal** | happens at the same time (`init()`) |
| **Procedural / communicational** | shares an order of execution, or the same data |
| **Functional** | does exactly one thing |

Functional is the target, and the test is verbal: describe what the module does in one
sentence. If the sentence needs "and", cohesion is low.

## What it shows up as

Almost every [[Code Smells|code smell]] is one of these two failing: duplicated code is
missing cohesion, a long parameter list is stamp coupling, feature envy is a method that
belongs to a different class. [[Metrics]] tries to count it directly, and
[[Complexity]] is the word for what happens when you lose the argument.

Applies past code, too: [[Microservices]] is this at deployment scale, and
[[Operating System Structure]] is why kernels are layered.
